verdict.rationale:
ROS 2's core architecture—pub/sub topics, services, actions, standard message packages, and static name remapping—lets application nodes talk to hardware-abstracted interfaces (e.g. a sensor driver publishing standard sensor_msgs) so swapping the underlying driver/node doesn't require touching the consuming application code (ros2-docs-20, ros2-docs-10, ros2-docs-31, ros2-docs-44, ros2-docs-25). Client libraries in multiple languages further decouple app logic from implementation (ros2-docs-7, ros2-docs-35).

missing for 10: explicit documentation framing this as a formal 'hardware abstraction layer' with interface-stability guarantees, first-party guidance/examples on swapping drivers without app changes, and independent/hands-on confirmation that real swaps happen cleanly (community evidence instead focuses on general ROS pain points, not this specific capability).
